subject: biology
topicDisplay: Theme D · Molecules (Replication, Protein Synthesis, Mutations)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: DNA replication is described as semi-conservative because each new molecule contains:
options: One original (template) strand and one new strand
questions.explain: Meselson and Stahl's experiment confirmed each daughter DNA keeps one parental strand.

questions.q: The enzyme that unwinds and separates the two DNA strands during replication is:
questions.explain: Helicase breaks the hydrogen bonds between bases to unwind the double helix at the replication fork.

questions.q: DNA polymerase adds new nucleotides only to the:
questions.explain: Because synthesis is 5'→3', one strand is made continuously (leading) and the other in fragments (lagging).

questions.q: On the lagging strand, DNA is synthesised as short fragments that are later joined by:
questions.explain: Ligase joins the Okazaki fragments of the lagging strand into a continuous strand.

questions.q: Free DNA nucleotides pair with the exposed template bases according to:
questions.explain: A pairs with T and C with G, ensuring each new strand is complementary to its template.

questions.q: Transcription is the process in which:
options: A gene's DNA is copied into messenger RNA
questions.explain: RNA polymerase synthesises mRNA complementary to the template DNA strand.

questions.q: Translation of mRNA into a polypeptide occurs at the:
questions.explain: Ribosomes read mRNA codons and assemble amino acids into a polypeptide.

questions.q: A codon is:
options: A triplet of mRNA bases coding for one amino acid
questions.explain: Each three-base codon specifies an amino acid or a start/stop signal.

questions.q: The molecule that carries a specific amino acid to the ribosome and has an anticodon is:
questions.explain: tRNA anticodons pair with mRNA codons, delivering the correct amino acid in sequence.

questions.q: The genetic code is described as 'degenerate' because:
options: Most amino acids are coded by more than one codon
Each amino acid has only one codon
Every codon is a stop codon
questions.explain: Multiple codons for the same amino acid reduce the impact of some point mutations.

questions.q: A gene mutation is:
options: A change in the base sequence of DNA
A folding error in a protein
The loss of a whole organelle
questions.explain: Gene (point) mutations alter the DNA base sequence and may change the protein produced.

questions.q: Sickle-cell anaemia results from a single base substitution in the haemoglobin gene, an example of a:
questions.explain: A single base change alters one amino acid (glutamic acid to valine), changing haemoglobin's behaviour.

questions.q: Inserting or deleting a single base often has a large effect because it causes a:
options: Change to only one amino acid
questions.explain: Frameshift mutations shift the reading frame, usually producing a very different, non-functional protein.

questions.q: CRISPR-Cas9 is a technology used for:
questions.explain: CRISPR allows targeted cutting and editing of DNA at chosen sequences, raising both possibilities and ethical questions.

questions.q: Agents that increase the rate of mutation, such as UV light and certain chemicals, are called:
questions.explain: Mutagens damage or alter DNA; some are also carcinogens that can lead to cancer.

questions.q: Why is accurate DNA replication essential before cell division?
options: Each daughter cell must receive a complete, correct copy of the genome
To reduce the number of chromosomes
To remove all mutations from the parent
questions.explain: Replication ensures genetic continuity; proofreading by DNA polymerase keeps error rates very low.

questions.q: If a template DNA strand reads 3'-TAC-5', the corresponding mRNA codon is:
questions.explain: mRNA is complementary and antiparallel to the template, and uses uracil; AUG is also the start codon.

questions.q: The start codon that signals the beginning of translation is:
questions.explain: AUG codes for methionine and marks the start; UAA, UAG and UGA are stop codons.

questions.q: A silent mutation has no effect on the protein because:
options: The altered codon still codes for the same amino acid
It always occurs in a stop codon
questions.explain: Thanks to the degenerate code, some base changes do not change the amino acid sequence.

questions.q: The overall flow of genetic information in a cell is usually summarised as:
questions.explain: This 'central dogma' describes transcription of DNA to RNA and translation of RNA to protein.
